questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My connection to the city was important to me, and my ability to study in german was a huge plus. I have lived in Berlin before and wanted to go back, and I also wanted to try to study there, as I am considering doing my Masters degree in Berlin.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a wonderful time and enjoyed every second of it. The only minus being that the paperwork before, during and after the mobility was quite a lot, and the communication between KU, HU and me was a bit confusing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, as the online portals of KU and HU are quite different and everything wasn't in one place.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a short introduction meeting for Erasmus students at the faculty, which was really helpful and created a great overview.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a personal connection for part of my stay, and for a month I found something on WG-gesucht. I think WG-gesucht is the best option, but it's still very difficult. For a short period of time it's fine though.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's just really hard to find something for a longer period of time. You should create a notification system on WG-gesucht so you'll be able to send your application letters to the apartment offers as fast as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were only two options connected to the university, and they were both really far away.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First of all I had to go to an office to get a PIN-code, so afterwards I could sign in to all the portals and get my student ID. For regestering for classes we actually just had to go to the first one and then decide if we wanted to take part or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were some intro-meetings via zoom before the start of the semester, where we were able to ask questions. Also we were able to contact the coordinator at the faculty if we had questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted to take some of the Berlin Perspectives courses, but I didn't get any of them. All the other courses were no problem at all though, I could basically just choose freely.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a good idea to just go to a bunch of courses in the first week and check out what you find interesting. You have a lot of possibilities. And maybe don't expect to get a spot in a Berlin Perspectives course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of really interesting courses, it was almost hard to choose. Also i loved that I could choose freely if I wanted to do an exam or not, and generally that I was able to create my schedule as I wanted it to be.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of my courses were in german, so this has to be taken into account:  You need to be able to speak german well in order to take part in the discussions. Generally, the courses were on a high academic level, but I think it was about the same as KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of discussion-based seminars which were quite different than what I'm used to at KU. But also classic lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
532835 Feminist Urban Geography
532836 Geschichte der Astrologie
532812 Verwundbare Körper des Politischen. Vulnerability revisited
532840 Techno Culture. Geschichte und Gegenwart elektronischer Tanzmusikkultur in Berlin
532810 Behinderung – Kultur - Wissen
532811 Sadismus mit und ohne Sade

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Techno Culture course was super interesting and well planned. It was a project seminar counting 15 points, so it was a lot of work but it paid off. Also Feminist Urban Geography was really interesting, and it was nice that it was planned as a block seminar with only 4 days in total.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My personal spending was higher than expected. The 120DKK extra was for renting a bike every month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a bit more expensive than expected, probably because of increased inflation. Public transport was less expensive than expected because I didn't know about the semester ticket, but also because of the 9Euro-ticket: I will be paid back the amount that differs to what I paid for my semester ticket for three months.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I know there were a lot of options, but I didn't use any of them, which was a personal choice. But a café or bar for students at the faculty would have been nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports, language courses, and some activities for Erasmus students around the city specifically.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't take part in any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to bars, bike around, sit by the water, go to clubs, go to festivals, go to the lakes when the weather is good, meet people on apps, go thrifting, go to flea markets, eat at a bunch of different restaurants. Specifically with the 9-euro-ticket it's also nice to go a bit out of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I knew it already, but also it doesn't differ from Copenhagen that much, except it being more open and international.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: This was actually a bit hard for me, except in the course where I was part of a study group. I used my own connections outside of the university, but also apps.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it's a very international city with so many different people and ways of living, and it's easy to meet people. Also just the queer community there is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you take courses in german, you should be prepared to speak it on a high level, or you won't get a lot out of it.
2. Start looking for housing early on, as it is probably the most tricky part about moving to Berlin.
3. Take time to enjoy everything the city has to offer every day, because of course it's the best city in the world. Especially the clubs on the weekends: Here I have my best memories.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really got to use my german language skills. But just meeting so many nice people and having so much fun every day and every weekend has been amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had a few stressful weeks were I had to do quite a lot of readings and assignments, so it's good to be organized from the beginning of the semester and do your assignments early, so you won't have to do them all at once.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
